title: The Redis 8 Data and Query Engine

questions.prompt: What did Redis 8 do with the capabilities formerly shipped as 'Redis Stack'?

options.text: Folded them (JSON, the Query Engine, probabilistic structures, time series) into Redis Open Source, and added Vector Sets

questions.explanation: Redis 8 integrated the former module features into Redis Open Source and introduced the new Vector Sets type, so these capabilities are available out of the box.

questions.prompt: What does the Query Engine let you do that core Redis alone cannot?

options.text: Query data by its content — secondary indexes, full-text, and vector search — not just by key

questions.explanation: Core Redis looks up values by key. The Query Engine creates secondary indexes over hashes/JSON so you can filter, full-text search, aggregate, and do vector search by content.

questions.prompt: Which statements are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: Native JSON lets you update individual fields by JSONPath
A Bloom filter has no false negatives but possible false positives
Vector Sets support similarity search for embeddings (AI/semantic search)

questions.explanation: JSON supports path-based updates, Bloom filters are approximate (no false negatives, possible false positives), and Vector Sets do similarity search. Probabilistic types are approximate by design, not exact.

questions.prompt: What are Vector Sets / vector search primarily used for?

options.text: Finding items whose embedding vectors are most similar to a query — semantic search, recommendations, and RAG

questions.explanation: Vector similarity finds items by meaning (via embedding vectors), which powers semantic search, recommendations, and retrieval-augmented generation for AI applications.

questions.prompt: The probabilistic structure that answers approximate set membership with no false negatives but possible false positives is a ______ filter. (one word)
questions.explanation: A Bloom filter can say 'definitely not present' or 'probably present' — never a false negative, but sometimes a false positive — using very little memory.

questions.prompt: Why prefer native JSON over storing a JSON string and using GET/SET?

options.text: You can read and update individual fields by path without deserializing and rewriting the whole document

questions.explanation: Native JSON with JSONPath lets you address and modify a single field server-side, avoiding the read-modify-write of a whole serialized blob.
